name: Aftermath, 15 December 2002

date.source: The results page's own dateline, "Wednesday, December 15th, 11:59 PM Pacific Time" — the fed's own roleplay deadline for the card, which is how it dated every results page. The day-of-week the fed printed does not fall on that calendar date; the date itself is the fed's own and is recorded as written.

matches.note: The ring announcer gives the time: "YOUR WINNER AT 5 MINUTES 29 SECONDS".

Won by unhooking the strap from the top of the ladder. The document's own commentary names the stipulation in passing ("this is a ladder match") rather than in a card header; the page carries no card headers at all.

notes: The document opens mid-way through its own first match, with no card header, match listing or credits block of any kind; the four contests below are the four the text itself carries from bell to bell.

name: CATASTROPHIC

date.source: The show's own header: "Lights Out Wrestling Presents: CATASTROPHIC / October 23rd, 2004 / Location: Philadelphia, PA"

matches.note: Aaron Rain was carried out by paramedics and Enigma walked out mid-match, leaving Tessa Windsor alone for the fall; the document stages neither as a formal elimination.
Retained: "Your winners and still LOW Tag Team Champions of the World . . . Delta Upsilon Iooota!"

Staged so that "if either Swift Payne, Deadly Mist or Viper win via pin fall, all three men are co-holders of the Realm Championship". Retained: "The winner of this match and still the LOW Realm Champion - THE DEMOND!"

matches.stipulation: 2 out of 3 Falls Match - Extreme Title
matches.note: A title change. Psymon took the first fall by choking Ramorez out, Ramorez the second, and the third on a count the document's own commentary calls controversial — Psymon's foot was on the rope and neither referee nor commentary saw it. "The winner, and NEW EXTREME CHAMPION, JUVIAN RAMOREZ!!!!!"

A multi-tier caged structure in which "The men will have to pin ONE of their advisories." A title change, declared narratively rather than by the ring announcer: the bell sounds, "the referee is seen raising the hand of a fallen Annihilation", and in the segment that follows he unhooks the belt from the wire lowering it and puts it round his waist — and then hangs on that same wire and dies on screen. The fed's own champion banner shows the World Championship vacant on captures from 8 December 2004.

notes: The show's own cold-open replays clips of Tessa Windsor, John Adams, The Demond, Swift Payne, Cobi Deekins, Psymon, Juvian Ramorez, Matt Meyhu, Annihilation, Eric Russo and Jason Ortiz; per the anti-double-count rule the replayed footage generates no appearance rows of its own.

date.source: The show's own opening: "On June 11th, 2002, a dream was born. And on June 11th, 2003, there is a risk that it will die" — the fed's own first-anniversary card.

eliminations.note: pinned with a Tornado DDT after Dax's own teammate Joseph Magnus let the count land rather than break it up
double brainbuster; Jason Warrior made the pin

matches.note: The show's own opening match: four LOW roster members against four free agents, entering two minutes apart. Billed stakes: the winner becomes LOW Aftermath Champion if already on the roster, or earns an LOW contract if a free agent. Jason Warrior's win is the fed's own record for how he became Aftermath Champion (reign low-aftermath-r001).

The fed's own segment index bills this match "Rose/Vinyard vs Starwind/Coral"; the show's own text names him in full, "Phoenix Rose and Derek Vinyard", and stages him coming into the tag team final off a van crash and leg surgery. Declared new champions: "We have a winner!!! We have NEW CHAMPIONS!!! Phoenix Rose and Derek Vinyard are Lights Out Wrestling's new and improved Tag Team Champions!!!!"
Cyrus Skar pins Canyon Thunders and earns a Realm Championship title shot against Jason Ortiz.

Billed "Big Daveylicious" throughout, identified in the same breath as "most of us just know him as Big D" — the fed's own shorthand this registry resolves to Donny Diamond. Wins by pinfall after Annihilation misses a top-rope move.
Won by escape rather than pinfall; earns Matt Robinson the next shot at the Xtreme Championship.
"The ref's hand comes down before Sean can throw his shoulder up! Scorpion wins!"
"Bottom line, we have a new champion! ... NEW XTREME CHAMPION! JUDGEMENT!!!" See reign low-xtreme-r005.
"That was three! ... Ring the bell, ref, this one's over, Kage won!" A grudge match between former Shadow Riders tag partners.

matches.stipulation: LOW World Championship, Sixty-Minute Iron Man Match
matches.note: Scored 2-2 (one fall each declared, plus a tied suicide-dive cover) when the sixty-minute limit expired; ring announcer Rusty Monarch declares a sudden-death continuation inside the cage. Before any sudden-death fall is scored, Jason Kage and Eric Russo (the Shadow Riders) run in, attack both men, and announce their own retirement from the ring in the same segment — the served text never returns to declare a winner of the title match itself. Left unresolved rather than guessed; World Champion Tristan Belmont's own reign (low-world-r004) is not shown ending here.

matches.stipulation: Loser Leaves LOW, ownership of Lights Out Wrestling
matches.note: The anniversary main event: Trigger (LOW's original owner) against Mike Meyhu (the mystery-CEO-turned-owner he'd been fighting all year). Tristan Belmont runs in and turns face, hitting Meyhu with the Battle Cry through the announce table before Trigger makes the cover for the finish: "IT'S OVER! TRIGGER HAS DEFEATED MIKE MEYHU! TRIGGER IS ONCE AGAIN OWNER OF LIGHTS OUT WRESTLING!"

name: Realm 23

date.source: The show's own text calls itself "the twenty-third edition of Lights Out Wrestling's Saturday Night Realm"; the page's own dateline reads "Saturday, January 18th, 11:59 PM Pacific Time", which is the fed's own roleplay deadline for the card rather than an explicit airdate, so the date is held at circa precision.

matches.note: A three-way the document bills as "a battle of the rookies" between Zurick and two men it names only "Chris" and "Miller" — LOW's own roster of the period carries a Chris Kinsley and a Chris Wrestling, and a Marcus Miller and a Miller Magnum, and nothing in the document resolves which. The two unresolved entrants are left out rather than guessed. Staged in a room rather than a ring, with no bell, but fought to a three-count.

Luke Justice is billed here as "The X-treme champion... with his title belt draped over his shoulder" and the document's own commentary calls the result "a giant upset over the Xtreme Champion" — but it never says the belt was on the line and never declares a title change. Won on a thirty-count, not a fall.
"The winner of this contest by way of Knockout.....JASON KAGE!!!!"

Explicitly non-title: "The next match is a non-title battle between two former friends" — Pax "is going into the match as the Aftermath champion, and he is sure to come out as Aftermath champion, whether he loses or wins".
A barbwire dome. The pre-show teaser spells the stipulation "Lighting Dome match"; the bell-time call spells it "Lightning Dome match".

notes: The document's own Table Of Contents is present but empty in the surviving capture; the source page's seven <a name="matchN"> anchors carry no readable labels, so the seven matches below are read from the text itself. The show's own cold-open "Last week..." package replays Lotus, PoGo, Mike Meyhu, Jesse Jamester, Tristan Belmont, Ezra, the Shadow Riders and Luke Justice; per the anti-double-count rule it generates no appearance rows.

name: Realm 29

date.source: The fed's own Realm Results page for the same week reads "Realm: April 08, 2003", and the fed filed this document under its own filename 040803. The document's own header line, "Sunday, April 6th, 11:59 PM Pacific Time", is the roleplay deadline for the card rather than the airdate — the same convention every LOW card page uses. The show's own text calls itself "the twenty-nineth edition".

matches.note: Won on a count-out with Devlin holding the ropes. Mid-match the referee announces "I was told a man MUST win here tonight in this match. There will be no draw."

Iron Lung is billed throughout as "the Aftermath Champion" and the document calls the belt "his newly won Aftermath Championship"; it never states the bout was for the title and declares no title change.
Fought in a junkyard; the document's own commentary adds "it is no holds barred". Annihilation is billed as the reigning Xtreme Champion; the belt is never said to be on the line.

Eric Russo is billed throughout as "the Realm Champion" — the fed's own bio cards date his Realm reign 2 February to 23 April 2003, and this show falls inside it. The document never states the bout was for the title.

Fought inside a cage the document describes but never names as a formal stipulation. Billed in pre-match commentary as "a triple threat match for the number one contendership to the WORLD TITLE"; the win sends Belmont to the pay-per-view against Mike Meyhu.

notes: The show opens on a poetic framing device ("Memories of last week...") and plays out, in full in-ring prose, two contests — Dark Haze over "Nightmare" Sean Dahmer, and Tristan Belmont over Mike Meyhu — before the broadcast restarts on "The lights are on... We have just entered the Realm... We have returned." All three of those men wrestle again later the same night, so the opening pair is the previous week's card replayed; per the anti-double-count rule neither generates a match or appearance row here.

date.source: The show's own header: "Realm / 8/02/03 / From Miami, Florida... / And now, Realm 41 with Jerry Donalo and Casey Sanders."

name: Realm 48

date.source: The show's own header: "Realm / 04/12/04 / And now, Realm 48 with Jerry Donalo and Casey Sanders."

matches.note: Fought up a ladder for the Realm Championship, which Skar retains — the document has him throw down "his Realm title" after unhooking the belt, and the fed's own champion banner already shows him as Realm Champion on captures from 28 March 2004. The bout sits before the show's own start marker ("The pyros explode on the entrance ramp as Realm forty-eight begins") and is interleaved with the new president's arrival, but the document never frames it as replayed footage and the commentary calls it live; recorded as a match of this show, with the placement noted.
Won by submission.
Won by escape.
"With both Legacy and Magnus locked in submissions from the Saikyo System, the ref watches and has no choice but to call for the bell."
Won by escaping the cage. The document's own commentary states there were "no titles on the line, only pride".
For the eXtreme Championship, which Iron Lung retains on a thirty-count. The document's own commentary calls it "the first time this title has been defended since we opened doors again".

notes: The show carries a Credits block, but it credits only "Card editor - LOW Staff" and names no per-segment writer, so the segment-by-segment index the fed's own 2003 pay-per-views carry is not available here.

name: Realm 49

date.source: The card's own second line reads "3/27/04", but that date precedes Realm 48's own "04/12/04" dateline despite the higher edition number, and the fed's own Realm archive index lists no 3/27/04 entry at all: a stale-template dateline, like the one this fed's own 15 December 2002 Aftermath page carries. The show falls after Realm 48 (12 April 2004) and before the 50th Realm (held here at 5 May 2004), so between 13 April and 4 May 2004; the card was live by its capture of 15 April 2004. April 2004 is the honest precision.

notes: An announced card, not a results page: the fed published the matches and a two-roleplay limit for the event, and no results page for this edition survives. No outcome is recorded for any of the five bouts.

matches.note: Billed "Warriors Match - eXtreme Title", Iron Lung defending. The document is an announced card and carries no result.
The document is an announced card and carries no result.
The document is an announced card and carries no result.
Billed "Number One Contenders to Realm Title". The document is an announced card and carries no result.
The document is an announced card and carries no result.

name: Wednesday Night Realm, 50th Edition

date.source: The show carries no dateline of its own — it bills itself only as "Wednesday Night Realm, 50th Edition!". Jason Kage's own bio card dates the Metallo Zords' Tag Team Championship reign "08/18/03 - 05/05/04", and this is the show on which the Metallo Zords lose those belts; the window the rest of the record allows — after Realm 48 of 12 April 2004, and by this page's own capture of 31 May 2004 — contains that date. Held at circa precision because the identification rests on that reading rather than on any dateline the document itself carries.

matches.note: One fall, pinfall or submission, with entrance music and pyro barred as a punishment. Ty Baron leaves as a result.
Won on a school-boy roll-up after Jason Ortiz ran in on Warrior.

For the Realm Championship, and awarded rather than won: after Skar attacked his own valet Jackie Bust the fed's own president suspended him mid-match — "the winner of this match, and NEW LOW Realm Champion, Malik Katsuya".
For the Tag Team Championship, won off the hook: "Grasping the titles Lotus throws one down to Raizo... The bell sounding, the match is over... The Saikyo System wins it!"

For the eXtreme Championship — "The winner of this match and new LOW eXtreme Champion---ANGELUS SORROW!" The card's own section header spells the stipulation "Ultimate Tapei Deathmatch"; the ring announcer spells it "Ultimate Taipei Match".

matches.stipulation: Six Man Fifteen Foot High Ladder Match
matches.note: For Primetime Central's own Global Championship, which Jesse Jamester carried into the match and Hessian carried out — "THE NEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEW PRIME TIME GLOBAL CHAMPION.... HESSIIAAAAAAAN!!!!!" The belt is PTC's, not LOW's.

notes: Three of LOW's own five championships changed hands on this show, and the fed's own champion banner corroborates all three: captures of 28 March 2004 show Cyrus Skar, the Metallo Zords and Iron Lung holding the Realm, Tag Team and Xtreme titles, and captures of 31 May 2004 show Malik Katsuya, Raizo and Angelus Sorrow holding them. The show's own closing credits read "Lights Out Wrestling 2003", a stock footer rather than a dateline.

date.source: The show carries no dateline of its own. The fed's own Realm 29 (8 April 2003) builds to it as next week's pay-per-view: "And next week at Shell Shock on Pay Per View... I'll prove that to the world"; the fed's own In The End (11 June 2003) recalls that Tristan Belmont "defeated Mike Meyhu and Jesse Jamester about two months ago at Shell Shock"; and the show's own opening, "For ten months, disaster has plagued Lights Out Wrestling", counts from the fed's founding in June 2002. Mid-April 2003; the day is not recorded. The page's only capture, of 24 May 2005, is when the Wayback Machine saw it, not when the show ran (an earlier reading dated it by that capture).

eliminations.note: submission to a chinlock/chain-reaction hold after Canyon Thunders wore him down
pinned after an unidentified masked man ran in, chaired Devlin, and arranged the cover
pinned after both men were down to a double ten-count and only Thunders beat it
rolled up in a schoolboy after escaping Thunders' own Thunder Cave submission
pinned with a finisher after Skar unwrapped a turnbuckle pad
pinned with the Silence, Skar's finisher, after kicking out of the Night Fall and the Insane Asylum
entered to no music or pyrotechnics; pinned with the Night Fall and a chair shot

matches.note: The show's own opening match, ahead of the numbered undercard below — nine men, one elimination at a time, the winner promised a shot at the Aftermath Championship. Cyrus Skar's win is followed immediately by a run-in beatdown from Playaz Inc (Statuz Quo and Duzza), billed in-fiction as having just left PCW.
The fed's own segment index bills this match "Ortiz vs. Stecchino"; the show's own text names him in full, "Jason Ortiz versus Tony Stecchino".

The fed's own segment index bills this match "Reality/Mayhem vs. Dane"; the show's own text names him in full, "Reality/Mayhem versus Eric Dane", and stages it for the number-one contendership to the Xtreme Championship.

The fed's own segment index bills this match "Lung vs. CTK"; the show's own text names him in full, "Iron Lung vs. Coach Tex Kelley" — Iron Lung's own former manager, come back for the Aftermath Championship he says he won himself.

date.source: The show's own header: "Wakeup Call / 8/31/03 / From Buffalo, New York..."

matches.note: A LOW Xtreme Championship defence. The fed's own page for this card has the Xtreme Championship “currently held by Iron Lung, who will face off against a competitor not even in LOW for a defense”, and says the bout was first booked title-versus-title, “where Lung would put on the line the Xtreme Championship as he is doing now, with the added bonus of Almasy adding the PTC Global Championship to the mix”. The finish is on the same page: Iron Lung's 7.0 frog splash, “One … two … THREE! The bell tolls … the official gathers the Extreme Title from the corner” — Iron Lung retained. PTCpedia's own 2008 revision of Seymour Almasy's article (/promotions/ptc/archive/ptcpedia-seymour-almasy-2008.html) tells the same night from the PTC side: “the two men would meet a few weeks later in Lights Out Wrestling with Lung's title on the line; Iron Lung won this rematch.”

name: War Wounds: The Battle Rages On

date.source: Bounded by the surviving title card's own capture, 9 February 2003.

evidence.source: a copy held in the workshop
evidence.note: The pay-per-view's own page survives as a title card and nothing else — "War Wounds: The Battle Rages On" over an empty body.
